summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, diabetes, antiphospholipid syndrome, and prior pulmonary embolism on warfarin was admitted for chest pain and flu-like symptoms. He tested positive for Influenza B, which caused a persistent cough leading to costochondritis. Workup ruled out acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, and pneumonia. His chest pain was managed with acetaminophen and short-term oxycodone, and cough with suppressants. He was treated for dehydration with IV fluids, and his subtherapeutic INR was monitored without adjustment. He remained stable, with improving symptoms, and was discharged home the following day with instructions to follow up on his INR and resume home medications including metformin and furosemide.
